gloss: see, look; perceive, see to; (niphal) appear; (hiphil) show; sight, appearance, vision
summary: רָאָה is to see: with the eyes, and from there to look at, to perceive and understand (“God saw that it was good”, Gen 1:4), to see to or provide (“God will see for himself the lamb”, Gen 22:8), to look on someone’s affliction so as to act (Gen 29:32; Exo 3:7), to undergo (“see corruption”, “see death”, Psa 16:10; 89:49), and to see what God shows in vision. Its niphal is to be seen, to appear, used of Yahweh and his glory appearing and of Israel appearing before him at the feasts (Deu 16:16); its hiphil is to show. Its nouns are what is seen: מַרְאֶה sight, appearance and vision, מַרְאָה vision and mirror, רֹאֶה the seer, the old name of the prophet (1Sa 9:9). Arabic raʾā, Ge’ez rəʾya and Sabaic rʾy say “see” too, with the same causative “show” and the same nouns for vision and mirror, and the Mesha stele uses it as Psalms do, of looking in triumph on one’s enemies.

words.gloss: see, look; perceive; see to, provide; (niphal) appear; (hiphil) show

stems.gloss: see, look at; perceive; see to, provide; experience

senses.definition: To have sight and use it: to see what is before the eyes. Its loss is blindness, and idols, which have eyes, cannot do it.

evidence.note: Eli’s eyes had begun to grow dim; he could not לִרְאוֹת.
Isaac was old and his eyes were too dim מֵרְאֹת.
Gods of wood and stone, “which neither see nor hear nor eat nor smell”.
“Eyes they have, and they do not see.”
Out of gloom and darkness the eyes of the blind shall see.
“The hearing ear and the seeing eye, Yahweh has made both of them.”

senses.definition: To turn the eyes on something on purpose: to look out over a land, to look on a sight, to look and take in what is there. Often joined with “lift up the eyes” or set beside הִבִּיט “look”.

evidence.note: “Lift up your eyes and look (וּרְאֵה) from the place where you are, northward and southward.”
Moses on Pisgah: “lift up your eyes … and look with your eyes, for you will not cross this Jordan.”
“Let me turn aside now and see this great sight (הַמַּרְאֶה), why the bush is not burnt.”
“Lift up your eyes on high and see who created these.”
“Look (הַבִּיטוּ) and see (וּרְאוּ) if there is any pain like my pain.”
Everyone bitten who looks at the bronze serpent shall live.
“Do not look at me, that I am dark.”

senses.definition: To see that something is so: to take it in with the mind as well as the eye, to judge, to find out. It is how God judges his own works good, and how men come to know what is happening.

evidence.note: “God saw the light, that it was good.”
God saw everything he had made, and behold, it was very good.
Yahweh saw that the evil of man was great in the earth.
“We have plainly seen (רָאוֹ רָאִינוּ) that Yahweh was with you.”
The woman saw that the tree was good for food.
Israel saw the great work Yahweh did on Egypt, and feared Yahweh and believed.
“My heart has seen much wisdom and knowledge”: the heart sees.
“I saw that wisdom excels folly as light excels darkness.”
“See now that I, I am he, and there is no god with me.”

senses.definition: To go and see how a thing stands, or to weigh what to do: see how someone fares, consider a course, see to a matter.

evidence.note: “Go now, see the peace of your brothers and the peace of the flock, and bring me word.”
“Know and consider (וּרְאִי) what you will do.”
“Know and see what word I shall return to him who sent me.”
“Yahweh look upon you and judge.”
“Now see to your own house, David.”
“I will go down now and see whether they have done altogether according to its cry … and if not, I will know.”

senses.gloss: look on (with regard), take note of affliction
senses.definition: Of God above all: to see the affliction or need of his people so as to act for them. It stands beside “hear their cry”, “know their sorrows” and “remember”, and is the ground of deliverance.

evidence.note: “I have surely seen (רָאֹה רָאִיתִי) the affliction of my people … and heard their cry … for I know their sorrows, and I have come down to deliver them.”
Leah names Reuben: “because Yahweh has looked on (רָאָה בְּ) my affliction.”
God saw the sons of Israel, and God knew.
Hannah: “if you will indeed look on the affliction of your handmaid and remember me.”
Hagar names Yahweh “a God of seeing”: “have I here seen after him who sees me?”
The people heard that Yahweh had seen their affliction, and bowed and worshipped.
“See my affliction and my trouble, and forgive all my sins.”
“Remember, Yahweh, what has come upon us; look and see our reproach.”
Stephen quotes Exo 3:7: ἰδὼν εἶδον τὴν κάκωσιν τοῦ λαοῦ μου.

senses.definition: To see something out for oneself or another: to look out and pick, and so to provide. With לְ of the one provided for.

evidence.note: “God will see for himself (יִרְאֶה לּוֹ) the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.”
Abraham names the place יַהְוֶה יִרְאֶה, after the ram is found in the thicket.
“I have seen (רָאִיתִי) for myself a king among his sons.”
Saul: “See (רְאוּ) for me now a man who plays well, and bring him to me.”
“Let Pharaoh look out a man discerning and wise, and set him over the land.”
Gad “saw the first part for himself”, chose it.

senses.definition: Those picked out as fit for a purpose.

evidence.note: “The seven young women הָרְאֻיוֹת to be given her from the king’s house”: those seen fit, chosen.

senses.definition: To see life, good, evil, death or corruption: to live through it, to have it happen to one.

evidence.note: “What man lives and shall not see death, shall deliver his soul from the hand of the grave?”
“You will not give your holy one to see corruption (לִרְאוֹת שָׁחַת).”
Peter quotes Psa 16:10: ἰδεῖν διαφθοράν.
“Who is the man who desires life, loves days, to see good?”
Quoting Psa 34:13: ἰδεῖν ἡμέρας ἀγαθάς.
“I am the man who has seen affliction by the rod of his wrath.”
“See life with the wife whom you love.”
“Sword and famine we shall not see.”
“The years we have seen evil.”
Simeon would not see death (μὴ ἰδεῖν θάνατον) before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.

senses.gloss: look upon (with בְּ), in triumph or grief
senses.definition: With בְּ, to look on something to the full: on one’s enemies when they are overthrown, or on a disaster one cannot bear to watch.

evidence.note: “Yahweh is for me among my helpers, and I shall look on (אֶרְאֶה בְּ) those who hate me.”
“My eye has looked on my enemies.”
Of the enemy who said “Where is Yahweh your God?”: “my eyes shall look on her; now she shall be trodden down.”
“Do not look on (אַל־תֵּרֶא בְ) the day of your brother”, set beside “do not rejoice”.
“They look, they stare upon me (יִרְאוּ־בִי).”
Hagar: “Let me not look on the death of the child.”
“Lest I see the evil that will find my father.”

senses.definition: To see what God shows a prophet: the Lord on his throne, the visions of God, the signs he sets before him. Hence the participle רֹאֶה, the seer.

evidence.note: “I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up.”
“The heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God (מַרְאוֹת אֱלֹהִים).”
“I saw the Lord standing beside the altar.”
Micaiah: “I saw Yahweh sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven.”
“What do you see, Jeremiah?” “I see a rod of almond.” “You have seen well.”
“I saw by night, and behold, a man riding on a red horse.”
“I saw in the vision.”
Who say to the seers (לָרֹאִים), “Do not see”, and to the visionaries (לַחֹזִים), “Do not see for us right things.”
“The seven lampstands which you saw (εἶδες)”, answering Zechariah’s lampstand (Zec 4:2).

senses.definition: To see God, or someone’s face: to be admitted to his presence. No man can see Yahweh’s face and live, yet some are said to have seen God when he appeared by his angel; to see the king’s face is to come before him.

evidence.note: “You cannot see my face, for no man shall see me and live.”
“You shall see my back, but my face shall not be seen.”
Peniel: “I have seen God face to face, and my soul is delivered.” Hosea says he strove with the angel (Hos 12:5).
Manoah, once he knew it was the angel of Yahweh: “We shall surely die, for we have seen God.”
The elders saw the God of Israel.
“My eyes have seen the King, Yahweh of hosts.”
“Whom I shall see for myself, and my eyes shall behold, and not a stranger.”
“He shall not see my face”: Absalom lived in his house and did not see the king’s face.
“You shall not see my face unless your brother is with you.”

senses.definition: The imperative calling attention to what follows, almost “behold”: to a fact being declared or a thing given.

evidence.note: “See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which Yahweh has blessed.”
“See, I have set you over all the land of Egypt.”
“See, I have made you a god to Pharaoh.”
“See, I have set before you today life and good, and death and evil.”
“See, God is witness between me and you.”

senses.definition: A passive of the simple stem, once: what is seen, or not seen.

evidence.note: His flesh wastes away from sight, “and his bones that were not seen (רֻאּוּ) stick out”. Pointed as a qal passive.

senses.gloss: appear (of God, his angel, his glory)
senses.definition: Of Yahweh making himself seen: appearing to the fathers, in the bush, at the tabernacle in the cloud of his glory, and at his coming.

evidence.note: “Yahweh appeared to Abram … and he built there an altar to Yahweh who appeared to him.”
“The angel of Yahweh appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of the bush.”
“I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob as El Shaddai.”
“And the glory of Yahweh appeared to all the people.”
Yahweh appeared to Solomon the second time.
“Yahweh will rise upon you, and his glory will be seen upon you.”
“Who can endure the day of his coming, and who can stand when he appears (בְּהֵרָאוֹתוֹ)?”
“The God of glory appeared (ὤφθη) to our father Abraham.”

senses.definition: Of things: to come into sight or to be found anywhere.

evidence.note: “Let the waters be gathered into one place, and let the dry land appear.”
The tops of the mountains were seen.
The bow shall be seen in the cloud.
Unleavened bread for seven days: “no leavened bread shall be seen with you, nor leaven seen with you in all your borders.”
The channels of the sea were seen.
The flowers appear on the earth.
The ends of the poles were seen from the holy place, but not from outside.

senses.definition: To come and be seen before someone: Israel’s males before Yahweh at the three feasts, a man before the priest, Elijah before Ahab.

evidence.note: “Three times in the year all your males shall appear before Yahweh your God … at the feast of unleavened bread, the feast of weeks and the feast of booths; and they shall not appear before Yahweh empty.”
“None shall appear before me empty.”
Samuel brought “that he may appear before Yahweh, and abide there for ever”.
“When shall I come and appear before God?”
“When you come to appear before me, who required this from your hand?”
“He shall show himself to the priest a second time.”
“Go, show yourself to Ahab.”

senses.definition: The passive of “see to, provide”.

evidence.note: “As it is said to this day, In the mount of Yahweh it shall be seen (יֵרָאֶה)”, answering the name יַהְוֶה יִרְאֶה.

stems.gloss: show, cause to see; cause to experience

senses.definition: To make someone see a thing: a land, the way, a pattern, one’s treasures.

evidence.note: “Go … to the land that I will show you.”
“I have caused you to see it with your eyes, but you shall not go over there.”
“According to all that I show you, the pattern of the tabernacle.”
The lampstand was made “according to the pattern (מַרְאֶה) which Yahweh had shown Moses”.
In fire by night “to show you the way”.
“Show us the way into the city.”
Hezekiah showed them his treasure house.
When he showed the riches of his glorious kingdom.
“Show me, I pray, your glory.”

senses.definition: Of Yahweh showing a prophet what he is to see.

evidence.note: “Thus he showed me: behold, the Lord standing on a wall made by a plumb line.”
“Yahweh showed me: behold, two baskets of figs.”
“Set your heart on all that I show you, for to show you have you been brought here.”

senses.gloss: cause to see = cause to experience
senses.definition: To make someone live through good or hard things, or look on his enemies’ fall.

evidence.note: “You have made your people see hard things; you have made us drink the wine of staggering.”
“You who have shown me many and evil troubles will revive me again.”
“Why do you make me see iniquity?”
“With length of days will I satisfy him, and show him my salvation.”
“Who will show us good?”
To make his soul see good in his labour.
“God will let me look on my enemies (יַרְאֵנִי בְשֹׁרְרָי).”

senses.definition: To be made to see: Moses shown the pattern, Israel shown that Yahweh is God, an infection shown to the priest.

evidence.note: “See, and make them by their pattern which you are being shown (מָרְאֶה) on the mountain.”
“According to its plan which you were shown on the mountain.”
“To you it was shown, that you might know that Yahweh, he is God; there is none else besides him.”
The infection “shall be shown to the priest”.
Quoting Exo 25:40: κατὰ τὸν τύπον τὸν δειχθέντα σοι ἐν τῷ ὄρει.

stems.gloss: look at one another; meet face to face

senses.gloss: look at one another; face one another (in battle)
senses.definition: To see each other: of men looking at each other at a loss, and of two kings meeting face to face to fight.

evidence.note: Amaziah: “Come, let us look one another in the face (נִתְרָאֶה פָנִים).”
They looked one another in the face at Beth Shemesh, and Judah was struck.
“Why do you look at one another?”

evidence.locator: רָאָה → εἴδω (aorist εἶδον) ×545, ὁράω ×108 (lemma counts, MACULA alignment); Exo.3.7, רָאֹה רָאִיתִי → ἰδὼν εἶδον; Psa.16.10, לִרְאוֹת → ἰδεῖν

evidence.note: Exo 3:7: ἰδὼν εἶδον τὴν κάκωσιν τοῦ λαοῦ μου.
Psa 16:10: οὐδὲ δώσεις τὸν ὅσιόν σου ἰδεῖν διαφθοράν.
Isa 6:9–10: βλέποντες βλέψετε καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδητε.
Isa 52:15: οἷς οὐκ ἀνηγγέλη περὶ αὐτοῦ ὄψονται.
Isa 64:3: ἃ ὀφθαλμὸς οὐκ εἶδεν.
Isa 40:5: καὶ ὄψεται πᾶσα σὰρξ τὸ σωτήριον τοῦ θεοῦ.
Psa 95:9: καὶ εἶδον τὰ ἔργα μου.

evidence.locator: רָאָה → βλέπω ×48 (lemma count, MACULA alignment); Isa.6.9, רְאוּ רָאוֹ → βλέποντες βλέψετε; 1Sa.9.9, רֹאֶה → βλέπων

evidence.note: “Seeing they do not see”, fulfilling Isa 6:9.

evidence.locator: רָאָה → ὀπτάνομαι ×169 (lemma count, MACULA alignment), chiefly the niphal; Gen.12.7, וַיֵּרָא → ὤφθη; Exo.23.17, יֵרָאֶה → ὀφθήσεται

evidence.note: “The God of glory appeared (ὤφθη) to our father Abraham.”
“There appeared (ὤφθη) to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai an angel of the Lord in a flame of fire in a bush” (Exo 3:2).
The risen Christ “appeared (ὤφθη) to Cephas, then to the twelve”.
“He shall appear (ὀφθήσεται) the second time, without sin, to those who eagerly wait for him, for salvation.”

evidence.locator: רָאָה → δεικνύω ×57 (lemma count, MACULA alignment), the hiphil and hophal; Exo.25.40, מָרְאֶה → δεδειγμένον; Exo.25.9, מַרְאֶה → δεικνύω

evidence.note: Exo 25:40: “according to the pattern shown (δειχθέντα) you on the mountain”.
Gen 12:1: εἰς τὴν γῆν ἣν ἄν σοι δείξω.
“Show us the Father” (compare Exo 33:18).

parallels.note: Seeing with hearing: the two senses God gave, which idols lack and the hardened will not use.

evidence.note: “Yahweh has not given you a heart to know, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, to this day.”

parallels.note: Seeing leads to knowing: see and know, or see in order to know.

evidence.note: “That they may see and know, and consider and understand together.”

parallels.note: “Look and see”: the deliberate look beside the seeing.

evidence.note: “Do not look (תַּבֵּט) at his appearance … man sees (יִרְאֶה) to the eyes.”

parallels.note: The other verb for seeing, above all in vision: רֹאִים beside חֹזִים.

evidence.note: Samuel הָרֹאֶה, Nathan the prophet, Gad הַחֹזֶה.

opposites.note: The blind, who do not see; Yahweh opens their eyes.

evidence.note: “Look, you blind, that you may see.”

opposites.note: Hidden from sight, against what is seen.

evidence.note: “You shall see my back, but my face shall not be seen.”
“He hides his face; he will never see.”

phrases.gloss: appear before Yahweh (at the three feasts)
Yahweh will see (to it), will provide

words.gloss: sight, appearance, look; a sight; vision

senses.definition: How someone looks, often with “good” or “beautiful”: the outward appearance, which man sees and God looks past.

evidence.note: “Do not look at his appearance (מַרְאֵהוּ) … for man looks on the eyes, but Yahweh looks on the heart.”
“You are a woman beautiful of appearance (יְפַת־מַרְאֶה).”
Joseph was beautiful of form and beautiful of appearance.
Their appearance was better and fatter than the youths who ate the king’s portion.
“His appearance was so marred, more than any man.”
“He has no form nor majesty that we should look at him, and no appearance that we should desire him.”
Pharaoh’s cows, fair and ugly of appearance.

senses.gloss: appearance (of a thing), what it looks like; כְּמַרְאֵה “like the look of”
senses.definition: The look of a thing: the sign a priest reads in a skin disease, the fire on the tabernacle, the glory on the mountain, and in Ezekiel and Daniel what the heavenly things looked like, said with care as “the appearance of the likeness of”.

evidence.note: If “the appearance of the infection is deeper than the skin of his flesh, it is the infection of leprosy”.
On the tabernacle at evening “as the appearance of fire until morning”.
“The appearance of the glory of Yahweh was like a consuming fire on the top of the mountain.”
“As the appearance of the bow in the cloud … this was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of Yahweh.”
His face “as the appearance of lightning”.
“Their appearance is as the appearance of horses.”

senses.gloss: sight, what the eyes see; a sight
senses.definition: What is seen, or the seeing of it: a spectacle, what pleases or maddens the eye, a pattern shown.

evidence.note: “Let me turn aside and see this great sight.”
Every tree “pleasant to the sight and good for food”.
“You shall be mad from the sight of your eyes which you shall see.”
The branch of Jesse “shall not judge by the sight of his eyes, nor reprove by the hearing of his ears”.
“Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of desire.”
“Walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes; but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.”
The lampstand made “according to the מַרְאֶה which Yahweh had shown Moses”: the sight shown him, the pattern.

senses.definition: What a prophet sees from God, and its meaning to be understood; and Moses, to whom Yahweh spoke openly, “in sight and not in riddles”.

evidence.note: “Gabriel, make this man understand the vision (הַמַּרְאֶה).”
“He understood the word, and had understanding of the vision.”
“The appearance of the vision which I saw was like the vision which I saw when I came to destroy the city.”
“Mouth to mouth I speak with him, and in sight (וּמַרְאֶה), and not in riddles; and the form of Yahweh he beholds.”

evidence.locator: מַרְאֶה → εἶδος ×19 (lemma count, MACULA alignment); Isa.53.2, מַרְאֶה → εἶδος; Num.12.8, מַרְאֶה → εἴδει

evidence.note: The holy Spirit descended σωματικῷ εἴδει, as a dove.
At the transfiguration the εἶδος of his face was altered.
“You have neither heard his voice at any time nor seen his εἶδος”, where Num 12:8 says Moses saw Yahweh מַרְאֶה, εἴδει.
“We walk by faith, not by sight (εἴδους).”

evidence.locator: מַרְאֶה → ὄψις ×18 (lemma count, MACULA alignment); 1Sa.16.7, מַרְאֵהוּ → ὄψιν

evidence.note: “Do not judge according to appearance (κατ᾽ ὄψιν), but judge righteous judgment”: 1Sa 16:7 and Isa 11:3.
“His ὄψις was as the sun shining in its strength.”

evidence.locator: מַרְאֶה → ὅραμα ×4 (lemma count, MACULA alignment); Exo.3.3, הַמַּרְאֶה → τὸ ὅραμα

evidence.note: Moses “wondered at the ὅραμα” of the bush: Exo 3:3.
“Tell the ὅραμα to no one until the Son of man is risen from the dead.”
He who sat on the throne was “like a jasper and a sardius stone ὁράσει, and a rainbow round the throne like an emerald ὁράσει”, as Ezekiel’s כְּמַרְאֵה (Ezk 1:28).

parallels.note: “The appearance of the likeness”: Ezekiel’s guarded description of what he saw.

opposites.note: Man sees the appearance, Yahweh the heart.

senses.definition: A seeing given by God, by night or in waking: the way Yahweh makes himself known to a prophet, set beside the dream.

evidence.note: “If there is a prophet among you, I Yahweh make myself known to him in the vision (בַּמַּרְאָה); I speak with him in a dream.”
“God spoke to Israel in the visions of the night.”
Samuel was afraid to tell Eli the vision.
“I saw visions of God.”
“I Daniel alone saw the vision, for the men with me did not see the vision.”

senses.definition: A looking glass of polished bronze, the thing one sees oneself in.

evidence.note: He made the bronze basin “of the mirrors (בְּמַרְאֹת) of the serving women who served at the door of the tent of meeting”.

evidence.locator: מַרְאָה → ὅρασις ×3 and ὅραμα ×2, κάτοπτρον ×1 (Exo 38:8) (lemma counts, MACULA alignment); Ezk.1.1, מַרְאוֹת → ὁράσεις

evidence.note: “Your young men shall see ὁράσεις.”
“Thus I saw the horses ἐν τῇ ὁράσει.”

words.summary: The qal participle used as a title: the old name of the prophet, the man to whom one went to inquire of God.

senses.definition: One who sees what God shows: Samuel, Hanani. Scripture itself says it is the older name of the prophet.

evidence.note: “Formerly in Israel, when a man went to inquire of God, he said, Come, let us go to the seer; for the prophet of today was formerly called the seer.”
“I am the seer … and I will tell you all that is in your heart.”
Samuel the seer.
Samuel הָרֹאֶה beside Nathan the prophet and Gad הַחֹזֶה.
Hanani the seer rebukes Asa.
The plural participle: “who say to the seers (לָרֹאִים), Do not see.”

senses.definition: The act of seeing, in Hagar’s name for Yahweh: the God who sees her.

evidence.note: “You are אֵל רֳאִי, a God of seeing; for she said, Have I here also seen after him who sees me?”

senses.definition: How someone looks; and of a wasted body, its look or flesh that can be seen.

evidence.note: David was ruddy, “with beautiful eyes and good of appearance (טוֹב רֹאִי)”.
“His flesh wastes away from sight (מֵרֹאִי).”

senses.definition: Something set up to be stared at in its shame.

evidence.note: Of Nineveh: “I will cast filth on you and make you vile, and set you as a spectacle (כְּרֹאִי).”

words.summary: Once, in Job, of a cast metal mirror; the same thing as מַרְאָה in Exo 38:8.

senses.definition: A mirror of cast metal, hard and bright, to which the sky is compared.

evidence.note: “Can you with him spread out the skies, strong as a cast mirror (כִּרְאִי מוּצָק)?”

words.summary: Once, in the read text (Qere) of Ecc 5:10; the written text has the same letters as the infinitive.

senses.definition: The mere seeing of what one owns, all the owner gets from wealth that others eat.

evidence.note: “When goods increase, they increase who eat them; and what profit is there to their owner, except the seeing (רְאוּת) of his eyes?”

words.summary: Once, in Isa 28:7, the same letters as רֹאֶה “seer” but read as the act of seeing: the priest and prophet “err in vision”. Its tokens are counted under רֹאֶה “seer”, so it has no key of its own here.

senses.definition: The seeing a prophet does, which drunkenness corrupts, set beside judgment.

evidence.note: “Priest and prophet reel with strong drink … they err in vision (בָּרֹאֶה), they stumble in judgment.”

words.summary: Read as an adjective in one verse only, Job 10:15 (וּרְאֵה עָנְיִי, “and seeing my affliction”), beside “full of shame”; the same letters are the verb’s imperative “and see my affliction”. Its tie to the root is plain; whether it is an adjective at all is not, and its tokens are counted under the verb.

senses.definition: One who looks on his own affliction.

evidence.note: “If I am righteous I will not lift my head, full of shame and seeing my affliction.”

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic, twice in Daniel, of the look of the image and of the fourth man in the fire. The letters are the Aramaic form of the root, with the guttural lost.

senses.definition: How something or someone looks, terrible or godlike.

evidence.note: The great image stood before the king, “and its appearance (וְרֵוֵהּ) was terrible”.
“The appearance (וְרֵוֵהּ) of the fourth is like a son of the gods.”

cognates.gloss: see with the eye; see with the mind, judge, opine; experience
cognates.note: Lane’s sources give the seeing as of several sorts: with the eye, by supposition, by consideration, and with the mind; and رَأَى مِنْهُ كَذَا “he experienced such a thing from him”. These answer to the Hebrew’s seeing with the eyes, perceiving and judging (Gen 1:4; Ecc 1:16) and seeing as undergoing (Psa 89:49). The verbal noun رَأْي is a judgment or opinion, “a thing that a man has seen with his mind”.
Originally أَرْأَى: “I made him to see the thing; i.e. I showed him the thing”, with أَرِنَا مَنَاسِكَنَا “show us our rites”. The same causative as the Hebrew hiphil הֶרְאָה (Gen 12:1; Exo 25:9).

cognates.gloss: (form VI) see one another; of two bodies of men, face each other
cognates.note: “They saw one another”; تَرَاءَى الجَمْعَانِ “the two bodies of people saw each other”, approached and faced each other: the reciprocal answering to the hithpael “let us look one another in the face” of two kings meeting in battle (2Ki 14:8, 11).

cognates.gloss: a dream, a vision in sleep
cognates.note: A noun of the verb: “a dream, or vision in sleep”, with رَأَى فِى مَنَامِهِ رُؤْيَا “he saw in his sleep a vision”. It answers to מַרְאָה “vision” (Gen 46:2 “visions of the night”; Num 12:6, beside the dream) and to the prophet’s seeing.

cognates.gloss: aspect, look, outward appearance; beauty of aspect
cognates.note: رِئْيٌ and مَرْآةٌ (with a-vowel) “aspect, look, or outward appearance … whether beautiful or ugly”, and the former also “beauty of aspect”: the same as מַרְאֶה and רֳאִי “appearance”, with or without “good, beautiful” (Gen 12:11; 1Sa 16:12).
With i-vowel, the instrument of seeing: “a mirror”, originally مِرْأَيَةٌ. The same formation and sense as מַרְאָה in Exo 38:8, and רְאִי in Job 37:18.

cognates.gloss: apt, fit, worthy (of a thing); more fit
cognates.note: هُوَ مَرْآةٌ بِكَذَا “he is apt, meet, suited … or worthy of such a thing”, and أَرْأَى “more, and most, apt, meet”. This may answer to Est 2:9 הָרְאֻיוֹת, the young women “seen fit” to be given to Esther. Recorded as possible: one Hebrew use, and Lane gives no account of how the sense comes from seeing.

cognates.gloss: see; see visions; look at, consider; (causative) show
cognates.note: Dillmann gives videre, absolute and with an object, with “see that” and “see whether”; videre visiones (Gen 41:1 and Joel 3:1 in the Ge’ez Bible, ርእይ “vision”, Dan 7:1); spectare, intueri; and providere vel eligere, “provide or choose for oneself or another”, as Hebrew רָאָה לְ (Gen 22:8; 1Sa 16:1). The causative አርአየ is “cause to see”, monstrare, ostendere, as the hiphil.

cognates.gloss: see, experience; (h-stem) show, especially an oracular vision; (noun) oracular vision
cognates.note: Sabaic (Old South Arabian). The verb is “see > experience”: “the sign he saw in the temple”, “when they saw that the disease was approaching”, “may the god see (and punish) him”, “they did not experience the calamity”. The causative hrʾy is “cause to see > show, specifically an oracular vision” (“according to what the god had shown his servant in his sleep”), and the nouns rʾy and hrʾyt are an oracular vision. The particle rʾ “now, indeed” is probably the frozen imperative “behold!”, as Hebrew רְאֵה is used (Gen 27:27; Deu 30:15).

evidence.locator: pp. 473–474, RʾY (verb, h-stem, nouns rʾy and hrʾyt); p. 473, Rʾ (particle)

cognates.gloss: (causative) let me look upon; (simple) look upon
cognates.note: Moabite, the Mesha stele. Line 4, כי השעני מכל השלכן וכי הראני בכל שנאי, “for he had saved me from all the assailants, and because he had caused me to look upon all my foes”; line 7, וארא בה ובבתה, “and I looked upon him and upon his house”, of Omri’s son. The same construction with בְּ as the Psalms’ “I shall look on those who hate me” (Psa 118:7) and “God will let me look on my enemies” (Psa 59:11).

doctrine.statement: Hagar, fleeing Sarai, names Yahweh “a God of seeing (אֵל רֳאִי)” (Gen 16:13); Leah names her son because “Yahweh has looked on my affliction” (Gen 29:32); Hannah asks him to “look on the affliction of your handmaid” (1Sa 1:11). At the bush he says, “I have surely seen the affliction of my people … and I have come down to deliver them” (Exo 3:7–8), and Stephen repeats it (Act 7:34). Each time his seeing is set beside hearing, knowing and remembering, and is followed by his acting (Exo 2:24–25; 4:31). From the verses: when scripture says Yahweh sees his people’s affliction, it means he has taken it in hand; it is the ground of their deliverance, not a bare observation.

Abraham tells Isaac “God will see for himself the lamb for a burnt offering” (Gen 22:8), and when the ram is found in Isaac’s place he names the place יַהְוֶה יִרְאֶה, “as it is said to this day, In the mount of Yahweh it shall be seen” (Gen 22:13–14). Hebrews says Abraham offered up his only son, reckoning that God was able to raise him even from the dead, and received him back in a figure (Heb 11:17–19); John the Baptist points to Jesus as “the Lamb of God” (Joh 1:29); Paul writes that God “did not spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all” (Rom 8:32); and Jesus says Abraham rejoiced to see his day, “and he saw it, and was glad” (Joh 8:56). From the verses: the lamb God would see to was not found in Abraham’s day, when a ram took Isaac’s place; it was provided in God’s own Son, and the promise “in the mount of Yahweh it shall be seen” looked forward to it.

Yahweh tells Moses, “You cannot see my face, for no man shall see me and live” (Exo 33:20), and John and Paul say that no one has seen God at any time, whom no man has seen or can see (Joh 1:18; 1Ti 6:16). Yet Jacob says “I have seen God face to face” where Hosea says he strove with the angel (Gen 32:31; Hos 12:5); Manoah, knowing “it was the angel of Yahweh”, says “we have seen God” (Jdg 13:21–22); and at the bush “the angel of Yahweh appeared” and spoke as God (Exo 3:2–6; Act 7:30–32), the angel of whom Yahweh says “my name is in him” (Exo 23:21). Jesus says, “He who has seen me has seen the Father” (Joh 14:9), and of the faithful, “they shall see his face” (Rev 22:4; Mat 5:8; 1Jo 3:2). From the verses: God himself has not been seen by men; he has been seen in those who bear his name, his angels and finally his Son; and to see his face is promised to those made like him.

Isaiah is sent to say, “See indeed, but do not perceive”, and to shut the people’s eyes “lest they see with their eyes … and turn and be healed” (Isa 6:9–10); Moses says Yahweh had not given Israel “eyes to see” to that day (Deu 29:3), and Jeremiah and Ezekiel speak of a people who have eyes and do not see (Jer 5:21; Ezk 12:2). Jesus says his parables fulfil Isa 6:9–10 (Mat 13:13–15), John applies it to those who did not believe his signs (Joh 12:40), and Paul to the Jews of Rome (Act 28:26–27). From the verses: to “see” in scripture is to perceive and respond; a people can look on God’s works and not see them, and that blindness is itself a judgment.

The psalmist asks, “What man lives and shall not see death, shall deliver his soul from the hand of the grave?” (Psa 89:49): to see death is to undergo it, and no man escapes it. David says, “You will not leave my soul to the grave, nor give your holy one to see corruption” (Psa 16:10). Peter and Paul argue that David died, was buried and saw corruption, so the words were spoken of the Christ, whom God raised, and who did not see corruption (Act 2:27–31; 13:35–37). From the verses: death is the common lot of every man, the soul included; Christ alone was kept from corruption, by resurrection, and his resurrection is the hope set out of the grave.

When Samuel looked on Eliab, Yahweh said, “Do not look at his appearance … for man looks on the eyes, but Yahweh looks on the heart” (1Sa 16:7). Of the branch from Jesse it is said, “he shall not judge by the sight of his eyes” but with righteousness (Isa 11:3–4); and the servant had “no appearance that we should desire him”, his appearance marred more than any man’s (Isa 53:2; 52:14). Jesus says, “Do not judge according to appearance, but judge righteous judgment” (Joh 7:24). From the verses: what the eye sees of a man is not what God judges by, and the one he chose to judge the world was one whose appearance men despised.

At the feasts of Lev 23 that called Israel up to the sanctuary, unleavened bread, weeks and booths, “all your males shall appear (יֵרָאֶה) before Yahweh your God in the place which he shall choose, and they shall not appear before Yahweh empty” (Deu 16:16; Exo 23:14–17); through the feast of unleavened bread no leaven was to be seen (Exo 13:7). The psalmist longs, “When shall I come and appear before God?” (Psa 42:3), and Isaiah condemns those who come to appear before him with unclean hands (Isa 1:12–15). Malachi asks who will stand “when he appears” (Mal 3:2), and Hebrews says that Christ has entered heaven itself “now to appear before the face of God for us”, and will appear a second time for salvation (Heb 9:24, 28). From the verses: to appear before Yahweh was to come into his presence at his appointed times with an offering and clean hands; Christ now appears there for his people, and they wait for his appearing to them.

note: Drafted 2026-11-13. BDB keys claimed: t.ab.aa (verb), t.ab.am (מַרְאֶה), t.ab.ak (מַרְאָה), t.ab.ac (רֹאֶה seer), t.ab.ai (רֳאִי), t.ab.ah (רְאִי), t.ab.ag (רְאוּת, no tokens: Ecc 5:10 רְאוּת is untagged in the database), xt.aa.ab (Aramaic רֵו). Left unclaimed because their tokens are the same as another key’s: t.ab.al (מַרְאָה “mirror”, the same 11 tokens as t.ab.ak; Exo 38:8 is cited under the mirror sense of מַרְאָה); t.ab.ad (רֹאֶה “vision”, the same 14 tokens as t.ab.ac; the word is kept without a key, Isa 28:7); t.ab.ab (adjective רָאֶה, whose 32 tokens are all the verb’s imperative וּרְאֵה; the word is kept without a key, Job 10:15). Names left for name entries: רְאוּבֵן and gentilic רְאוּבֵנִי (t.ab.ap, t.ab.aq; names/reuben.json), רְאָיָה Reaiah (t.ab.ao), יִרְאִיָּיה Irijah (t.ab.an), הָרֹאֶה Haroeh (t.ab.ae, 1Ch 2:52); places: בְּאֵר לַחַי רֹאִי (Gen 16:14; 24:62; 25:11, counted in t.ab.ai). Zero-token cross-references: t.ab.af רַאֲוָה (Ezk 28:17 לְרַאֲוָה, entered as a qal infinitive), t.ab.aj, t.ab.ar, j.dg.ab, m.di.af, xt.af.ab. Left out as belonging to other roots: הָרָאָה, an unclean bird (Deu 14:13), filed under דאה (d.ad.ab); מֻרְאָה “crop” (Lev 1:16), filed under מרא (m.di.ac); the brief’s וַיִּרְאוּ tokens analysed as ירא. Ezk 40:4 and Exo 25:9 מַרְאֶה are hiphil participles of the verb, not the noun. The niphal “appear before Yahweh” (Exo 23:17; 34:23; Deu 16:16; Isa 1:12; Psa 42:3) is read as the text is pointed; the consonants could be qal “see the face of Yahweh”, as Psa 42:3 (וְאֵרָאֶה) and Isa 1:12 (לֵרָאוֹת) may have been read; not settled here. Cognate gaps: no Ugaritic word for “see” from this root in Segert or Fisher (Ugaritic uses phy, ḥdy); none in Krahmalkov for Phoenician; Akkadian sees with amāru, naṭālu, and no cognate was found; Syriac and Jewish Aramaic see with ḥzā, so the Peshitta has no word of the root and the Aramaic רֵו is the only Aramaic form. Arabic رِئَة “lung” (Lane n14336) is under the same Arabic letters but answers to no word in scripture. Leads not followed: Leslau’s Comparative Dictionary of Ge’ez for rəʾya (page not checked). Open questions: (1) the hophal מָרְאֶה (Exo 25:40) and hiphil participle מַרְאֶה (Exo 25:9; Ezk 40:4) are pointed like the noun; the brief counts some under both; (2) whether רֳאִי in Gen 16:13 is the noun “seeing” or the participle “who sees me” (both readings sit in the verse); (3) the doctrine “seeing-god” states God-manifestation through the angel and the Son: check the framing.
